title: Agent-designed detector uses fewer measured baseband cycles at unresolved error-rate difference
summary: A Claude coding agent designed a platform-specific signal detector and tested its implementation on commercial baseband silicon. It used34010 cycles per frame versus39520 for the ported reference, a13.9% reduction. The error-rate evaluation could not resolve a difference between them; this is a bounded hardware-specific algorithm result, not an over-the-air network benefit.
organization: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence; NXP Semiconductors; RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual structural/model Methods, specific result evaluation and source caveats

evidence.tested: The new ec_frozen detector reuses a frozen inverse as a preconditioner, with measured platform profiles guiding agent structural choices. Cycle counts were reproduced exactly on silicon.
evidence.unknown: One campaign and reduced workload dimensions limit transfer to the original large detector. Error intervals overlap and stored outcomes do not permit a fully paired comparison. No real radio-channel, power or network-level improvement was measured. Human constraints and frozen evaluators shaped the design; generic porting/coding speedups are not the represented discovery.
evidence.ai_role: The agent selected the new detector structure from measured hardware costs, rather than only implementing a fully specified human algorithm.
